title: C1604 — Ignition coil-on-plug 4 connector guide
introduction:
A coil-on-plug ignition coil produces the high voltage needed for a spark at its spark plug. I read its connector map like an address book: the cavity identifies the position, and the circuit row explains who that position connects to. A familiar-looking housing alone cannot tell the whole story.

Start with the connector identity table, then match the drawing’s cavity labels to the Cavity column. Read across the applicable row for its circuit, color, gauge, function and terminal reference. Check the engine entry in Qualifier before comparing the control-circuit rows. The supply rows retain the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative.

This guide explains the reference, including the separate pigtail listing. It does not teach physical access, disconnection, probing, wire selection or replacement. The physical viewing side, gauge convention and meanings of the Size and Used codes are unspecified here. The summary Pin Count disagrees with the drawing and pigtail cavity listing; that discrepancy remains unresolved.

edits.why: I use the housing outline to keep the supplied drawing recognizable: the rounded body has projections on the left, with the cavity labels stacked vertically. The shaded middle position corresponds to the row without an assigned circuit or terminal. Those projections have no identified release function, and the drawing does not label a physical viewing side.

edits.text: Read the cavity and circuit assignments
edits.why: The engine qualifier distinguishes the control-circuit entries; read each applicable row as a complete package rather than mixing its gauge or terminal reference with another row. The supply entries describe the same fuse-or-circuit-breaker function but have different gauge entries and blank qualifiers, so their order cannot establish engine applicability. Blank circuit fields indicate that no circuit assignment is given for that position, not a fault-test result.

The pigtail table connects the kit listing with its Service Part and Engineering Shell references. I keep those distinct from Terminal Part Number in the circuit table: they identify different parts of the connection. The pigtail gauge and material entries describe the listed service item; they do not supply a wire-selection or splice procedure.

originalAuthorHold: The summary Pin Count differs from the cavity count shown by the drawing and pigtail listing. Confirm what Pin Count represents; the evidence does not justify treating assignment rows as additional physical cavities.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 33 primary units, both complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. Pin Count and unqualified supply-gauge applicability ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
